q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 303-1, how is the minimum number of boreholes found for a structure whose footprint is more than 500 m²?
o: 2 + A/1000, rounded up to the next whole number
ref: NSCP 2015 Sec. 303.1 and Table 303-1 Minimum Required Number of Boreholes
n: For footprints over 500 m², the minimum is 2 + A/1000 rounded up, where A is the footprint area in m². Smaller footprints need 1 borehole (up to 50 m²) or 2 (50 to 500 m²). These are minimums; the geotechnical engineer may ask for more.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to submerged clay?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Submerged soil is lighter than dry or damp soil because buoyancy offsets part of its weight; use it for soil below the water table.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 205-1, what minimum live load applies to residential decks?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 205-1 Minimum Uniform and Concentrated Live Loads
n: Residential decks take the same 1.9 kPa as the basic floor area. Exterior balconies are higher, at 2.9 kPa, because crowds gather along the edge.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 304-1, what allowable foundation pressure applies to sandy gravel or gravel (GW and GP)?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 304-1 Allowable Foundation and Lateral Pressure
n: Sandy gravel and gravel are allowed 100 kPa, with lateral bearing of 30 kPa per metre of depth. Sands and silty or clayey gravels drop to 75 kPa, and clays to 50 kPa.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to dry gravel?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Dry gravel weighs about 16.3 kN/m³, heavier than clean dry sand (14.1) because the coarser grading packs more solid per volume.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 205-1, what minimum live load applies to school corridors above the ground floor?
o: 4.8 kPa, plus a 4.5 kN concentrated load
3.8 kPa, plus a 4.5 kN concentrated load
1.9 kPa, plus a 4.5 kN concentrated load
2.4 kPa, plus a 9.0 kN concentrated load
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 205-1 Minimum Uniform and Concentrated Live Loads
n: Upper-floor school corridors are 3.8 kPa; ground-floor corridors, which take the full crowd at dismissal, are 4.8 kPa. Both carry a 4.5 kN concentrated load.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 305-1, what minimum footing width and thickness apply to a foundation supporting one floor?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 305-1 Minimum Requirements for Foundations
n: For one floor: 150 mm foundation wall, 300 mm footing width, 150 mm footing thickness and 300 mm depth below undisturbed ground. Each extra floor adds to all of these (two floors: 375 mm wide, 175 mm thick, 450 mm deep).

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to wrought iron?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Wrought iron is slightly heavier than cast iron (70.7) and slightly lighter than cold-drawn steel (77.3).

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 205-1, what minimum live load applies to office lobbies and ground-floor corridors?
o: 4.8 kPa, plus a 9.0 kN concentrated load
2.4 kPa, plus a 9.0 kN concentrated load
2.9 kPa, plus a 9.0 kN concentrated load
3.8 kPa, plus a 4.5 kN concentrated load
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 205-1 Minimum Uniform and Concentrated Live Loads
n: Office lobbies and ground-floor corridors are designed for 4.8 kPa because everyone passes through them. General office floors are 2.4 kPa; all office rows carry a 9.0 kN concentrated load.

q: When may the prescriptive footing sizes of NSCP 2015 Table 305-1 be used without a separate design?
o: For any building of any height
Only for light buildings on ordinary soil, unless a foundation investigation calls for something else
Only for buildings on expansive soil
Only for footings under steel columns
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 305-1 Minimum Requirements for Foundations
n: Table 305-1 covers light buildings of one to three floors on ordinary ground. Where unusual conditions or expansive soils are found, or loads are heavier, the footings must be designed under Section 305.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to ashlar marble masonry?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Marble is one of the densest building stones. Ashlar granite and crystalline limestone are listed at 25.9 kN/m³.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what must be done to existing footings that may be undermined by a new excavation next to them?
o: Nothing, if they belong to a neighbour
They only need to be photographed before digging
They must be underpinned or otherwise protected against settlement and lateral movement
ref: NSCP 2015 Vol. 1, Chapter 3 (Earthworks and Foundations), Sec. 302.3.1
n: Sec. 302.3.1 requires existing footings that may be undermined to be underpinned adequately or otherwise protected against settlement and lateral movement. The owner of the new work must notify the adjoining owner before excavating.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to brass?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Brass (copper and zinc) is heavier than steel (77.3 kN/m³); copper itself is listed at 87.3.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to clean, dry sand?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Clean dry sand is 14.1 kN/m³. River sand, dry, is heavier at 16.7 because its grains are better graded and pack tighter.

q: Under NSCP 2015, to what minimum density must fill be compacted?
o: 80% of maximum density by ASTM D1557
90% of maximum density by ASTM D1557
ref: NSCP 2015 Vol. 1, Chapter 3 (Earthworks and Foundations), Sec. 302.4.4
n: Sec. 302.4.4 requires fill compacted to at least 90% of the maximum density from ASTM D1557 (modified Proctor), with at least three field density tests per 500 m² in every lift.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to ceramic tile?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Ceramic tile, at 23.6 kN/m³, is as heavy as reinforced concrete. For floor finishes NSCP also gives per-area loads in Table 204-2.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to tin?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Tin (72.1 kN/m³) is a little heavier than cast iron (70.7) and lighter than steel (77.3).

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 303-1, how many boreholes are required at minimum for a structure with a footprint of 50 m² or less?
ref: NSCP 2015 Sec. 303.1 and Table 303-1 Minimum Required Number of Boreholes
n: A footprint up to 50 m² needs at least 1 borehole; 50 to 500 m² needs 2; and above 500 m² the count is 2 + A/1000, rounded up.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to dry clay (earth, not submerged)?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Dry clay is light at 9.9 kN/m³ because of its open structure; damp clay is listed at 17.3.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 205-1, what minimum live load applies to the basic floor area of residences?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 205-1 Minimum Uniform and Concentrated Live Loads
n: 1.9 kPa (about 40 psf) is the basic residential floor load. Balconies are 2.9 kPa.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 304-1, what allowable foundation pressure applies to intact tuffaceous sandstone?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 304-1 Allowable Foundation and Lateral Pressure
n: Intact tuffaceous sandstone (unconfined strength at least 3 MPa and RQD above 70) is allowed 1,000 kPa, with lateral bearing of 300 kPa/m. Lightly weathered tuffaceous sandstone drops to 500 kPa.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to submerged sand or gravel and clay?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Submerged mixtures of sand or gravel and clay are 10.2 kN/m³, a little more than submerged sand or gravel alone (9.4).

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 205-1, what minimum live load applies to residential storage areas?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 205-1 Minimum Uniform and Concentrated Live Loads
n: Residential storage is 1.9 kPa, the same as the basic floor. Warehouse storage in Table 205-1 is far higher: 6.0 kPa light and 12.0 kPa heavy.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 304-1, what allowable foundation pressure applies to sands and silty or clayey gravels (SW, SP, SM, SC, GM, GC)?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 304-1 Allowable Foundation and Lateral Pressure
n: This group is allowed 75 kPa, with lateral bearing of 25 kPa/m and a sliding coefficient of 0.25. Clean gravels get 100 kPa and clays 50 kPa.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to ice?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Ice is lighter than fresh water (9.8 kN/m³), which is why it floats. The value is used for ice loads on structures.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 205-1, what minimum live load applies to school ground-floor corridors?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 205-1 Minimum Uniform and Concentrated Live Loads
n: Ground-floor school corridors are 4.8 kPa, higher than upper-floor corridors (3.8 kPa) and classrooms (1.9 kPa).

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 305-1, what minimum footing width applies to a foundation supporting two floors?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 305-1 Minimum Requirements for Foundations
n: For two floors: 200 mm foundation wall, 375 mm footing width, 175 mm footing thickness and 450 mm depth below undisturbed ground.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to lead?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Lead is the heaviest material commonly listed, at 111.5 kN/m³; it matters for radiation-shielded rooms such as X-ray suites.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 205-1, what minimum live load applies to general office floors (other offices)?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 205-1 Minimum Uniform and Concentrated Live Loads
n: Ordinary office space is 2.4 kPa (50 psf). Call centers are higher at 2.9 kPa because of their dense seating.

q: A building has a footprint of 1,600 m². Under NSCP 2015 Table 303-1, how many boreholes are required at minimum?
ref: NSCP 2015 Sec. 303.1 and Table 303-1 Minimum Required Number of Boreholes
n: Above 500 m², the minimum is 2 + A/1000 rounded up: 2 + 1.6 = 3.6, which rounds up to 4.
steps: A = 1,600 m², which is more than 500 m²

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to masonry grout?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Grout for filling hollow masonry cells is 22.0 kN/m³, close to plain concrete (22.6).

q: Under NSCP 2015, beyond what depth must an excavation or open cut have designed shoring or support?
ref: NSCP 2015 Vol. 1, Chapter 3 (Earthworks and Foundations), Sec. 302.3.3
n: Sec. 302.3.3 requires excavations or open cuts deeper than 1.5 m to have adequately designed shoring or support to protect against collapse.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to cast-stone masonry (cement, stone and sand)?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Cast stone is a concrete product, so its density matches plain stone concrete, 22.6 kN/m³.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to dry river sand?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: River sand, dry, is 16.7 kN/m³, heavier than clean dry sand (14.1).

q: What is a field density test used for in earthworks?
o: To find the bearing capacity of rock
To measure the slump of concrete
To check the in-place density of compacted fill against the laboratory maximum
To find the water table depth
ref: NSCP 2015 Vol. 1, Chapter 3 (Earthworks and Foundations), Sec. 302.4.4
n: Field density tests (such as the sand-cone test, ASTM D1556, or the nuclear gauge) measure how dense the placed fill really is. The result is compared with the laboratory maximum density to confirm the 90% requirement.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to plain concrete with stone aggregate?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Plain stone concrete is 22.6 kN/m³. Adding reinforcing steel raises it to 23.6 kN/m³.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to fresh water?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Fresh water is 9.8 kN/m³ (1,000 kg/m³ × 9.81 m/s²). Sea water is heavier at 10.1 because of its dissolved salts.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 303-1, how many boreholes are required at minimum for a footprint of more than 50 m² and up to 500 m²?
ref: NSCP 2015 Sec. 303.1 and Table 303-1 Minimum Required Number of Boreholes
n: Footprints from 50 to 500 m² need at least 2 boreholes, placed within the footprint and spread across it. Each should reach at least 5 m into hard strata or a suitable bearing layer.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to dry, packed sand and gravel?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Packing raises the density: dry loose sand and gravel is 15.7 kN/m³, dry packed is 17.3, and wet is 18.9.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 205-1, what minimum live load applies to residential exterior balconies?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 205-1 Minimum Uniform and Concentrated Live Loads
n: Balconies are 2.9 kPa, above the 1.9 kPa basic floor, because people crowd along the rail and the balcony is a cantilever with no redundancy.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 304-1, what allowable foundation pressure applies to lightly weathered tuffaceous sandstone?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 304-1 Allowable Foundation and Lateral Pressure
n: Lightly weathered tuffaceous sandstone (unconfined strength at least 1 MPa and RQD above 50) is allowed 500 kPa, with lateral bearing of 150 kPa/m, half the value for intact rock.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to glass?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Glass is 25.1 kN/m³, a little heavier than reinforced concrete. It governs the dead load of glass floors and skylights.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 205-1, what minimum live load applies to school classrooms?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 205-1 Minimum Uniform and Concentrated Live Loads
n: Classrooms are 1.9 kPa with a 4.5 kN concentrated load. The corridors outside them are heavier: 3.8 kPa upstairs and 4.8 kPa on the ground floor.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 304-1, what allowable foundation pressure applies to clays and silts (CL, ML, MH, CH)?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 304-1 Allowable Foundation and Lateral Pressure
n: Clays and silts get the lowest value, 50 kPa, with lateral bearing of 15 kPa/m, and no increase is allowed for a wider footing.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to cast iron?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Cast iron is 70.7 kN/m³, lighter than wrought iron (75.4) and steel (77.3).

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 205-1, what minimum live load applies to call centers and business-processing offices?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 205-1 Minimum Uniform and Concentrated Live Loads
n: Call centers and BPO offices are 2.9 kPa, above ordinary offices (2.4 kPa), because of their closely packed workstations. This row is a Philippine addition to the table.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 305-1, what minimum depth below undisturbed ground applies to footings supporting three floors?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 305-1 Minimum Requirements for Foundations
n: For three floors: 250 mm foundation wall, 450 mm footing width, 200 mm footing thickness and 600 mm depth. These are minimums; in practice footings are often set deeper.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to hydrated lime, compacted?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Hydrated lime is a light powder: 7.1 kN/m³ compacted and less when loose.

q: Under NSCP 2015, how steep may a cut slope be without a geotechnical report?
o: No steeper than 1 vertical to 2 horizontal (50%)
No steeper than 1 vertical to 1 horizontal (100%)
No steeper than 2 vertical to 1 horizontal
Any slope, if it is covered with grass
ref: NSCP 2015 Vol. 1, Chapter 3 (Earthworks and Foundations), Sec. 302.2.2
n: Sec. 302.2.2 limits cut slopes to 1V:2H (50%) unless a geotechnical report shows that a steeper cut is stable. Cuts must also be protected against erosion.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to aluminum?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Aluminum, at 26.7 kN/m³, is about one-third the weight of steel (77.3), which is why it suits curtain-wall framing.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to plywood?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Plywood is about 5.7 kN/m³. Particle board is listed a little heavier.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what is the maximum thickness of each lift when placing compacted fill?
ref: NSCP 2015 Vol. 1, Chapter 3 (Earthworks and Foundations), Sec. 302.4.4
n: Fill is placed and compacted in lifts no thicker than 20 cm, so the roller's compaction reaches the whole layer. Each lift must reach 90% of ASTM D1557 maximum density.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to portland cement, loose?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Loose portland cement is 14.1 kN/m³ (about 1,440 kg/m³), the figure used for cement storage and silo loads.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to cold-drawn steel?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Steel is 77.3 kN/m³ (about 7,850 kg/m³), the value used for structural steel and reinforcing bars.

q: Under NSCP 2015, for which structures is an exhaustive geotechnical study required?
o: Only structures ten storeys or higher
ref: NSCP 2015 Vol. 1, Chapter 3 (Earthworks and Foundations), Sec. 303.1
n: Sec. 303.1 requires an exhaustive geotechnical study to find in-situ soil parameters for structures two storeys or higher, with boreholes set by Table 303-1.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to reinforced concrete with stone aggregate?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Reinforced stone concrete is 23.6 kN/m³, the standard figure for the self-weight of slabs, beams and columns.

q: Under NSCP 2015 Table 204-1, what minimum design density applies to sea water?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 204-1 Minimum Densities for Design Loads from Materials
n: Sea water is 10.1 kN/m³, heavier than fresh water (9.8) because of dissolved salts. It is used for tanks and marine structures.
